The best trips don’t just change your location. They change what you want to return to.

Hi & welcome if your new here 👋🏽✨ I’m Saxon a 24 year old creative & storyteller & I think it’s about time I give a little introduction. 

I was born & raised in a cozy small beach town in Australia, it’s called Byron Bay. I’ve been taking photos & crating since I was around 12 years old. I’m highly passionate about capturing life from my perspective & I love to write/read inspiring words. 📸📝

Over the years my work has evolved from landscape photos, marine life, people, sunsets, quotes & id like to say it’s now in a place of all combined which is quite special. 
When did you discover my work? Let me know ?

Why I create? 
I will create no doubt for the rest of my life, it’s my passion & I’m blessed to have been doing it most my life so far! 🦋
Recently I’ve had quite a bit of success over here on instagram which has been humbling & exiting. 
But behind the scenes the work can be time consuming & tiring. Until I started receiving beautiful messages from you guys. Hearing how much these posts have had a positive impact on your days truly fills my heart 🫀 
So I’m at this beautiful stage in my life where I feel a pull inwards to create inspiration & post that inspire me most & or make me question life the most & then share with you guys. 

I hope this posts reaches you well & I would love for you to know how much appreciate you all for choosing to follow & view my work. This is mostly the “why” in what I do now ♾️ 
With that said, I came up with the beautiful idea recently to start my letter club, where once a month I send you a postcard, a story & a gift. Sharing a letter of inspiration that you can slow down with/be preset & find inspiration off of your phone <3
If this speaks to you comment “soulful” & I’ll DM you more info.

Once again, thank you 😊 your support has truly changed my life & I look forward to continuing to bring inspiration to your days ⏳

Big love
Saxon 🤍

Japan is one of the most photogenic places in the world yet so many people dont make it out of Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto. Here are some of the photos I have taken in over 10 trips to Japan with the locations as you swipe across the carousel! Such a gorgeous place and I hope you get out there and explore too! Huge thanks to @tk_north for the first photo! #japan #photography #tokyo

Sunset at lake kawaguchiko is so stunning and was lucky enough to see some paid actor fishing men!

You can’t go wrong with cherry blossom season! Spotted the perfect car to swing by at the right time with some morning light.

Hokkaido Japan is just an otherworldly place especially in winter. I’ve never seen a landscape quite like it

Okinawa Japan has one of the most incredible aquariums in the world. I know aquariums get a bad wrap but this one is humongous and does a lot for marine research. Regardless im only here to document life!

Nothing like Tokyo Tower!

I spent 3 days trying to photograph the Zao snow monsters because these eerie snow covered trees are so high up that the weather was extremely unpredictable even on perfect sunny days. Glad to the perseverance paid off!

More blossoms and iconic Japanese trains!

Almost midnight in the tiny town of Furano, Hokkaido. I was one of the only people out and about during a snow storm and the conditions were just wild.

this was our lovely tour guide: @tsaatan_reindeer_herders

these were our hosts Nyamka & Buyanaa for a night, a herder/nomad family next to the Tsagaannuur lake. It was their first time receiving travellers as guests and we had such a beautiful experience with them.

woke up to the smell of homemade bread and butter, it was such a peaceful morning.

this goat was stealing the show on all the pictures haha

traditional mongolian “Ger” with the moon and a beautiful sunset in the background

to get to one of the last existing nomadic reindeer tribes in northern mongolia, it took us many days of traveling through remote areas. we had to do the last stretch on reindeer back as no cars can reach their settlement.

one of the shamans of the tribe, her name is Tsegtseg

We visited her and some of the nomad families to ask questions and learn about their way of living. As we didn’t have any connection we just enjoyed the fresh air and beautiful nature around us

We had the pleasure to be the first visitors of their spring camp this season as they also just moved from their winter camp (they move approximately 6-8 times per year, to stay in colder places so their reindeers can find food and it doesn’t get too warm for them)

the men of the tribe chit chatting during golden hour

we stayed two nights sleeping in tepees (called Urts), where we took shifts in waking up during the night to add more wood to the fire to keep warm. You can imagine how cold it can get at night as it’s super close to Siberia.

they boil the snow they collect from the ground to make drinking water

The first morning we helped releasing the reindeers so the herders of the tribe could take them up the mountains to the areas with snow for them to feed.

the nomad family in their traditional clothing called “deel”

From Murun we visited a school in Tunel village because our tour guide was giving an english lecture at the local school (not part of the tour, we just asked if we can join since we arrived early).

petting baby goats after we took a little break from horse riding along the lake (i was in heaven)

had to capture this because the colors just looke

「本望年月消前念（běn wàng nián yuè xiāo qián niàn），奈何往事终难远（nài hé wǎng shì zhōng nán yuǎn）。」 - I once hoped time would erase the thoughts of yesterday. Instead, it taught me that some memories are never meant to fade. They settle quietly within us, 「凝成清愿伴流年（níng chéng qīng yuàn bàn liú nián）」, becoming a silent wish that walks beside us through the passing years. Perhaps healing was never about forgetting. It was about accepting that every place, every face, and every farewell leaves behind a gentle light, one that no longer weighs upon the heart, but softly illuminates the road ahead. What remains after time.
